## Overview

Pesticide poisoning is a priority indicator for injury mortality surveillance in South Africa, given its established role as a leading method of self-harm in rural/agricultural settings globally [@mew2017]. This page describes the epidemiology of pesticide poisoning deaths recorded in the national vital registration (VR) system, restricted to the **four ICD-10 codes StatsSA validates for pesticide poisoning specifically** — StatsSA MACOD 2022, Table 4.12 (interim definition, pending confirmation against the 2023 MACOD release), checked by Debbie Bradshaw. This is a deliberately **narrower** scope than a generic "poisoning" analysis (which would also include drugs, alcohol, gases and other chemicals under X40–X49/X60–X69/X85/Y10–Y19): each of the four codes below maps to pesticides specifically, one per intent category.

| ICD-10 code | Category | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|
| X48 | Accidental / unspecified | Unintentional pesticide exposure *or intent not documented on DNF* (ICD-10 default) |
| X68 | Self-harm | Intentional self-poisoning by pesticides |
| X87 | Assault | Pesticide poisoning inflicted by another person |
| Y18 | Undetermined | Intent unknown or not specified (pesticide poisoning) |

::: {.callout-important}
## Caution: intent categories reflect ICD-10 coding defaults, not certified intent

South Africa's death notification form (DNF) **does not include a field for manner of death**, contrary to the WHO-recommended Medical Certificate of Cause of Death [@groenewald2023importance]. Under ICD-10 Volume 2 coding rules, when manner of death is not stated by the certifier, external cause deaths are assigned to the most appropriate code by default [@who2016icd10] — in practice this can route to **either** the Accidental or the Undetermined code depending on how the cause was documented and coded, and the empirical pattern differs markedly by cause.

**For pesticide poisoning specifically, the dominant code is "Undetermined" (Y18), not "Accidental."** In this dataset, Y18 accounts for roughly **three-quarters of all pesticide poisoning deaths**, versus about a quarter for X48 (Accidental/unspecified) and only a few percent for X68 (Self-harm); X87 (Assault) is vanishingly rare. This is the opposite pattern to many other external-cause categories (e.g. Groenewald et al. (2023) found 98.7% of Stats SA firearm deaths coded accidental, versus 88.5% homicide on forensic NCoDV review [@groenewald2023misclassification]) and is consistent with the international literature on pesticide self-poisoning: non-forensic certifiers are often unable or unwilling to certify suicidal intent without a clear circumstantial history (e.g. a note, witnessed ingestion, psychiatric history), so many genuine self-harm pesticide deaths are likely coded Y18 rather than X68 [@mew2017; @prinsloo2017].

**Interpretation:** The large **Y18 (Undetermined)** share in these data should **not** be read as "intent unknown and therefore unimportant" — it most plausibly contains a substantial number of unrecognised self-harm deaths, consistent with pesticides' known role as a common suicide method. **X48 (Accidental)** likely also contains some genuine self-harm and a small number of assault deaths absorbed by the same DNF manner-of-death omission. Accurate intent-stratified estimates require triangulation with forensic mortality surveillance (NCoDV), Poisons Information Centre call records, and other independent sources [@prinsloo2024].
:::

### Deaths by intent

The **"Undetermined" (Y18, green)** category dominates — the opposite pattern to many other external causes, where the ICD-10 default assigns an accidental code whenever manner of death is not stated. For pesticides, non-forensic certifiers appear more likely to leave intent undetermined than to default to accidental — see the methodological note above [@groenewald2023importance; @who2016icd10; @mew2017].

## Age-group trends over time

### Age × year heatmap — nominal counts

Each cell shows the **absolute number of pesticide poisoning deaths** in that age band and calendar year. This reveals which groups contribute the most deaths in volume terms and allows direct comparison across time.

```{r}
#| label: fig-age-year-count-heatmap
#| fig-cap: "Fig. 9a. Annual pesticide poisoning deaths by age group (raw count). Darker = more deaths."
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 5.5

if (exists("fig_age_year_count_heatmap")) fig_age_year_count_heatmap else message("Run poisoning_wrangling.R")
```

### Age × year heatmap — proportional share

Each cell shows that age band's **share of that year's total pesticide poisoning deaths** (%). Using proportions rather than raw counts removes the effect of overall volume changes and isolates structural shifts in the age distribution — e.g. a darkening row signals a rising share for that group regardless of whether total deaths rose or fell.

```{r}
#| label: fig-age-year-heatmap
#| fig-cap: "Fig. 9b. Proportion of annual pesticide poisoning deaths by age group (heatmap). Darker = higher share. Each column sums to 100%."
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 5.5

if (exists("fig_age_year_heatmap")) fig_age_year_heatmap else message("Run poisoning_wrangling.R")
```

### Estimated annual percentage change (EAPC) by age group

The EAPC is derived from a log-linear regression of annual death counts on calendar year for each age band independently (with a 0.5 continuity correction for zero counts). It estimates the average year-on-year percentage change across 1997–2024. Red = increasing trend; blue = decreasing; faded points indicate *p* ≥ 0.05. This is the standard WHO / GBD approach for characterising mortality trends by subgroup.

```{r}
#| label: fig-age-eapc
#| fig-cap: "Fig. 10. EAPC by age group with 95% CI. Solid (opaque) points are statistically significant (p < 0.05). EAPC = estimated annual % change in pesticide poisoning death count, 1997–2024."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 6.5

if (exists("fig_age_eapc")) fig_age_eapc else message("Run poisoning_wrangling.R")
```

## Age-group trends by sex

The three figures below stratify the age-trend analysis by sex, enabling direct comparison between male and female pesticide poisoning death patterns — e.g. whether rising counts in older age groups are driven by males, and whether any increase in younger age groups is female-predominant.

### Age × year heatmap — counts by sex

Two side-by-side heatmaps showing raw death counts. Allows comparison of absolute burden between sexes across the age-year space.

```{r}
#| label: fig-age-year-sex-count
#| fig-cap: "Fig. 11a. Annual pesticide poisoning deaths by age group, stratified by sex (raw count). Each panel's colour scale is shared, so darker cells can be compared directly between male and female panels."

#| fig-height: 5.5

if (exists("fig_age_year_sex_count")) fig_age_year_sex_count else message("Run poisoning_wrangling.R")
```

### Age × year heatmap — within-sex proportional share

Each cell is the **percentage of that sex's total deaths** in that year falling in that age band. Proportions are computed separately within each sex, so the panels show whether the *age structure* of male and female pesticide poisoning deaths has shifted over time — independently of the overall sex ratio in deaths.

```{r}
#| label: fig-age-year-sex-prop
#| fig-cap: "Fig. 11b. Proportion of annual pesticide poisoning deaths by age group within each sex. Each panel's columns sum to 100%."
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 5.5

if (exists("fig_age_year_sex_prop")) fig_age_year_sex_prop else message("Run poisoning_wrangling.R")
```

### EAPC by age group — male vs female comparison

Log-linear EAPC estimated separately for each age group × sex combination. Blue circles = males; red triangles = females; faded = *p* ≥ 0.05. Reading across a row for a given age band shows which sex is driving any trend — and whether both sexes are changing in the same direction and magnitude.

```{r}
#| label: fig-age-sex-eapc
#| fig-cap: "Fig. 12. EAPC by age group and sex with 95% CI. Blue circle = male; red triangle = female. Faded = non-significant (p ≥ 0.05). Points are horizontally dodged for legibility."

#| fig-height: 6.5
```

## Years of Life Lost (YLL)

YLL is computed as the sum of remaining life expectancy at age of death across all registered pesticide poisoning deaths with a known, valid age and documented sex (male or female). Individual ages are mapped to WHO standard remaining life expectancy using linear interpolation of the WHO reference life table (Murray 1994; LE at birth = 82.5 years). Records with unknown age or unknown/other sex are excluded from this section but remain in the death-count analyses above.

::: {.callout-note}
## Reference life table

The WHO/GBD standard life table (Murray 1994) anchors YLL at a life expectancy of **82.5 years at birth**, providing a universal comparison benchmark independent of local South African life expectancy — which has fluctuated substantially over the study period due to HIV/AIDS and ART roll-out. Using a fixed standard means YLL reflects potential life lost relative to a best-practice survival frontier rather than current national survival. Standard values used for key ages: age 0 → 82.5 yr; age 20 → 62.8 yr; age 40 → 43.1 yr; age 60 → 24.3 yr; age 75 → 11.8 yr.
:::

### Summary

```{r}
#| label: tbl-yll-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Table 4. YLL by age group and sex — all pesticide poisoning deaths with valid age and known sex (1997–2024). YLL computed using WHO standard life table (Murray 1994). 'YLL/death' = mean standard life-years lost per registered death."

if (exists("tbl_yll_age_sex")) {
  flextable(as.data.frame(tbl_yll_age_sex)) |>
    bold(part = "header") |>
    theme_booktabs() |>
    fontsize(size = 9, part = "all") |>
    set_formatter(
      `Male YLL`    = function(x) formatC(x, format = "d", big.mark = ","),
      `Female YLL`  = function(x) formatC(x, format = "d", big.mark = ","),
      `Total YLL`   = function(x) formatC(x, format = "d", big.mark = ","),
      `Male deaths` = function(x) formatC(x, format = "d", big.mark = ","),
      `Female deaths` = function(x) formatC(x, format = "d", big.mark = ","),
      `Total deaths`  = function(x) formatC(x, format = "d", big.mark = ",")
    ) |>
    autofit()
} else {
  message("Run poisoning_wrangling.R")
}
```

### Mean YLL per death by age group

YLL per death declines monotonically with age because older decedents have fewer remaining standard life-years. The pattern reveals where the **per-death burden** is highest — typically in younger age groups — even when older groups contribute more deaths in absolute terms.

```{r}

#| fig-cap: "Fig. 14. Mean YLL per registered pesticide poisoning death by age group and sex. Reflects the WHO standard remaining life expectancy applied at each recorded age."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4.5

if (exists("fig_yll_per_death")) fig_yll_per_death else message("Run poisoning_wrangling.R")
```

## Death institution / place of death

The `DeathInst` field on the South African death notification form records where the death occurred. Values are: **Hospital** (1), **Emergency room / Outpatient** (2), **Dead on arrival** (3), **Nursing home** (4), **Home** (5), **Other** (6), **Unknown** (8), and **Unspecified** (9). For the broad grouping below, categories 1, 2, and 4 are combined as **Health facility**; category 3 (**Dead on arrival**) is kept separate because it implies the death occurred outside a facility but was certified at one; categories 5 and 6 form **Out of facility**.

::: {.callout-note}
## Unspecified records (code 9)

A substantial proportion of records carry code 9 (Unspecified). This likely reflects incomplete form completion rather than a genuinely unknown setting, and mirrors the broader data-quality limitations of the vital registration system. These records are retained in the tables below but excluded from the bar charts to avoid distorting the proportions of known categories. Their exclusion is reported in the figure footnotes.
:::

### X48: distribution by death institution

The chart below shows where accidental/unspecified pesticide poisoning deaths (X48) occurred, excluding the Unknown and Unspecified categories. The "Unspecified" share is shown in the table.

```{r}
#| label: fig-facility-acc

#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4

if (exists("fig_facility_acc")) fig_facility_acc else message("Run poisoning_wrangling.R")
```

```{r}
    autofit()
} else {

}
```

### Intent composition within each facility setting

The proportional stacked bars show how the intent mix varies across facility settings. "Undetermined" (Y18) is the dominant pesticide-poisoning intent code overall (see methodological note above), so settings where intent is hardest to certify are expected to show the highest proportional contribution from this category rather than "Accidental/unspec."

```{r}
#| label: fig-facility-intent
#| fig-cap: "Fig. 18. Intent composition of pesticide poisoning deaths within each facility setting (100% stacked bars). 'Other' intent excluded. Percentages are within-setting shares."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4

```

## Next steps

- Confirm/update this code definition once StatsSA publishes the 2023 MACOD release (current analysis uses the interim validated code set from the 2022 release, Table 4.12).
- Add population denominators to compute age-standardised mortality rates.
- Stratify provincial trends by intent.
- Link to external toxicology data (e.g. NPIS calls, emergency department presentations) for triangulation with IMS and NCoDV forensic data.
- Investigate the spike/dip years visible in the epicurve.
- Apply probabilistic redistribution of the "Accidental" category using forensic correction factors (e.g. from @groenewald2023misclassification) to obtain intent-adjusted estimates.
